text:
laura_sales: quick sync — ACME POC kicked off this morning. they filled most of the security questionnaire but reported very slow first-byte on the demo app (~2.3s) and occasional 429s. can we swarm? :grimacing:
omar_se: on it. do we have request IDs or metrics? is this happening on hosted or their dedicated infra?
acme_engineer: hosted. first token delay only for cold sessions. we see 429 spikes under moderate concurrency (~50rps). attaching last 3 logs
acme_engineer: ```
2026-03-20T09:14:22Z request_id=abc123 model=redwood-13b seq=0 status=200 latency_first_token_ms=2378
2026-03-20T09:14:23Z request_id=abc124 model=redwood-13b seq=0 status=429 error=rate_limit_exceeded
2026-03-20T09:14:24Z request_id=abc125 model=redwood-13b seq=0 status=200 latency_first_token_ms=2401
```
jinx_oncall: thanks. 2.4s TTFT sounds like cold KV cache + model spin-up. 429s at 50 rps could be backend queueing or our per-customer concurrency limit kicking in. i’ll check routing & limiter events.
sam_account_exec: they asked about pricing impact if we recommend keeping warm pools / dedicated bursts — can someone draft a quick estimate? they want to justify budget to finance.
omar_se: quick troubleshooting checklist: 1) check prefix/KV cache hit-rate 2) confirm batching config on their client (don’t force large synchronous batches) 3) verify request concurrency header and tokenization footprint
laura_sales: they used a naive client that sends 1 request/session with full context, no prefix seed. acme wants lowest latency for demos.
jinx_oncall: i pulled metrics — hostpool-id=host-7 has warmups disabled for that org. cache_miss_rate ~82% for recent requests. limiter logs show bursts of 429s around 09:14. looks like they hit ephemeral queue cap then fallback 429.
omar_se: action: enable client-side warmup and short prefix seeding; on our side enable per-org warm pool for demo window and temporary higher concurrency cap. tradeoff: higher cost for the time window.
acme_engineer: how fast can you flip those? demo scheduled 14:00 PT.
jinx_oncall: can do warm pool for 2 GPUs for the 2hr window. i’ll schedule now. need approval from infra budget owner?
sam_account_exec: approving temporary spike for demo. approximate cost delta: Omar, can you post estimate?
omar_se: estimate: extra warm pool 2xA100 for 2 hours ~ $120 (infra), plus additional tokens negligible for demos. if they later want dedicated reserved we can provide committed pricing.
laura_sales: perfect. sec question leftover: they flagged KMS integration + audit logs in questionnaire. security_bot, can you confirm standard approach and timeline for onboarding KMS for hosted?
security_bot: KMS onboarding (hosted) requires: 1) signed DPA addendum 2) customer provided key in supported KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault) 3) 3-5 business days for key binding and audit config. we can provide SOC2 artifacts. sending checklist in DM.
acme_engineer: thanks. for warmup, any client code sample? we can send a small warmup script.
omar_se: paste this quick warmup snippet — run from their app before demo:```bash
# seed prefix cache and KV
for i in 1..3; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","input":"Hello"}' &
done
wait
```
lara_sales: (typo: laura) :thumbsup:
jinx_oncall: i toggled warm pool on host-7 and bumped per-org concurrency from 30->80 for the 2.5hr window starting 2026-03-20T13:30:00-07:00. monitoring now.
acme_engineer: re-tested after warmup & bump: TTFT samples now ~180-220ms, no 429 in 10m smoke. huge improvement.
sam_account_exec: good outcome. next steps: 1) send pricing breakout to ACME 2) finish KMS onboarding docs 3) follow up recommendation: move to dedicated reserved if they need sustained low-latency
laura_sales: i'll send a short summary + cost estimate and attach security checklist. Omar/Jinx — can you both join a 30m post-demo retro tomorrow?
omar_se: yes
jinx_oncall: yes
acme_engineer: thanks everyone — demo confirmed at 14:00 PT. will report any anomalies.
laura_sales: closing the loop here: documented incident as "cold-cache + concurrency cap" and prep notes linked in handoff doc. :white_check_mark:
